title: ANSYS VM270 / TEAM23: permanent magnet and coil force

parameter_definitions.name: current
parameter_definitions.description: Signed winding DC current; the measured force target applies only to 0.05 A

parameter_definitions.name: displacement
parameter_definitions.description: Source axial displacement beyond the 0.127 mm spool end; source target applies to 0.234 mm

parameter_definitions.name: domain_radius
parameter_definitions.description: Radius of finite A=0 exterior adaptation; air mesh lengths are independent of radius

parameter_definitions.name: mesh_scale
parameter_definitions.description: Multiplier on body and local-air mesh lengths; exterior air remains fixed at 0.1 mm

assumptions: DC magnetostatics; source material laws are retained.
No external model or downloaded source script is executed.
Axisymmetric millimeter geometry follows the public ANSYS VM270 input dimensions, with a 280-turn series coil at 50 mA and axial magnetization.
Magnet permeability is calculated from the source input expression Br/(mu0*Hc), retaining Br=1.02 T and Hc=720000 A/m rather than the slightly inconsistent rounded printed permeability.
Brass and air have relative permeability one in this static model; the nonmagnetic spool has no separate magnetic interface.
The measured target 1.150*9.81e-3 N is retained; the table-rounded 0.0113 N and ANSYS numerical result 0.0112 N are separate comparisons.

Source infinite elements are replaced with an explicitly finite A=0 semicircle. Local and exterior air mesh lengths are independent of domain radius; numerical regions contain identical air and impose no physical boundary constraint.
The graded force-mesh settings were selected through recorded refinement; failed coarse force estimates remain in the audit.
limits: A passing target check is not a general convergence study or certification of a machine design.
Magnet weighted-stress force and coil Lorentz force must both match the signed measured targets, with an independent action-reaction and coil-estimator check.
Local stress-force estimates need much finer mesh than the coil Lorentz integral. A single solve is not a convergence certificate.
